capabilities: read EPUB, TXT, FB2, MOBI, AZW3, CBZ, and PDF books from a bookshelf with persisted progress
highlight and excerpt book passages into Markdown, Canvas, or Weave deck notes
jump two-way between book passages and the notes holding their excerpts
navigate books with TOC, bookmarks, and reference points
export chapters and excerpt notes to Markdown and expose a public API
disambiguation: Not a web-article or RSS reader; it reads local ebook files (EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, CBZ, PDF, TXT, FB2) imported from the vault.
extras: Freemium: reading, bookshelf, excerpts, and two-way tracing are free; Premium is a one-time purchase unlocking heatmap, Pomodoro timer, library timeline, vocabulary marking, and advanced Markdown export. Detailed tutorials, pricing, and privacy/premium-terms documents live on the external website (obsidian-weave.xyz). Part of a three-plugin Weave series (Reader, Deck, Incremental Reading) but works standalone.
motivation: To embed reading into the Obsidian knowledge workflow so excerpts and bookshelf data live in vault files rather than being locked inside a closed reading app.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to read ebook files in the vault or link note excerpts back to the exact book passage they came from.

relations.evidence: Deck adds spaced-repetition cards, incremental-reading calendar hooks, AI actions, and license inheritance.
Reading queue / calendar | Weave Incremental Reading (+ this plugin for EPUB chapter resume)

requires.name: Premium activation code (buy-once) for heatmap, focus timer, timelines, paragraph reading, and advanced export

summary: In-vault ebook reader with a bookshelf for EPUB, PDF, MOBI and other formats; highlights and excerpts save to notes with two-way links back to the book.
